content: Ligand 2 has the better drug-likeness (QED 0.883) but it is a 356 Da piperidine amide with a methyltetrazole and essentially no activity, and crossover would only shuffle two inactive scaffolds. Ligand 1 is far more useful than its Phi suggests: it is a small para-disubstituted benzene - a methyl at atom 0 on ring carbon 1, and a cyclobutyl ester at ring carbon 4 - which is exactly the substitution pattern I need, with two disposable groups para to each other and only 208 Da to start from. What this target rewards is an aryl-N(H)-azine link with a monocyclic azine whose ring nitrogen sits ortho to a free N-H, and the best version of that is a 4-methylpyridin-2-ylamino. Step 1 installs it: atom 1 is the aromatic carbon bearing the methyl at atom 0, a non-ring bond, so I cut the methyl off and attach the link there.
